t_advice_summary_textbox.text: From what I can gather, you are looking to pick the gnomes that will lead you to the forest with the most mushrooms.There are 2 forests, one bright and one dark, and different colours of gnomes. The gnomes coloured orange, red, green and blue will lead you to the bright forest containing a red basket, and the gnomes coloured brown, pink, purple and yellow lead you to the dark forest with a yellow basket.The key is to keep track of which forest gives you more mushrooms, as the forest that gives you more mushrooms changes per participant.the size of the gnome, their hat and where they are makes no difference, the important bit is to pay attention to the colour of the gnomes and figuring out which forest has the most mushrooms. As a reminder...Bright forest: red basket - orange, red, green and blue gnomesDark Forest: yellow basket - brown, pink, purple and yellow gnomesGOOD LUCK!! :)

vb_textbox.text: So without making this too complicated:There are 2 forests. The bright forest with a red basket which you get to my choosing the red, blue, green or orange gnomes. The dark forest with a yellow basket which you get to by choosing the yellow, brown, pink or purple gnomes.During each round (and I suspect possibly mid-round) the forest containing the most mushroom changes. so if initially your red basket was getting more mushrooms but suddenly starts getting 0, try the other forest and see if it has changed. If you pay attention then this becomes easier.bright forest/red basket: red, blue, green & orange gnomesdark forest/yellow basket: yellow, brown, pink & purple gnomesyou want to try and get the most mushrooms as you can. for the most part the forest was mostly consistent per round but there was once or twice that it changed mid round for me so just stay focused and you will be fine!! GOOD LUCK!!P.S. the position/hats/size of gnome doesn't make any difference, you're looking at the colour of the gnomes. you will get one bright forest gnome and one dark forest gnome on the screen at a time.
